messages:
incbot: ALERT: tenant_quantile_latency_high fired for tenant=acme-corp — 5xx_rate over SLA window, paging oncall
marie: ack — I'm on it, looking into customer impact now
marie: quick summary: only acme-corp hitting this check. User-facing symptoms: intermittent timeouts on write paths, not a full outage but degrading latency
ajay: looking at traces/logs — appears to be a burst that causes cache churn and some long tail tokenization CPU on a subset of hosts
ajay: preliminary hypothesis: high request-size + cold kv-cache -> downstream timeouts, not a global routing issue
ajay: proposal: tune the tenant-specific alert rather than global — raise threshold for enterprise-tier tenants and lengthen the evaluation window to avoid noisy flapping
ajay: proposed Prom rule (sketch):
```yaml
- alert: TenantHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=~"$TENANT",status=~"5.."}[10m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant=~"$TENANT"}[10m])) > 0.015
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/tenant-error-rate
```
siva: +1 to longer window. Also we should filter out internal/test tenants and our agent-bots (tenant !~ "^(staging|ci|bot)-")
siva: suggest adding a min-traffic guard: only fire if tenant_rps > 100 to avoid small-tenant noise
marie: ops: can we mute pages for acme-corp while we iterate? this is noisy and is generating duplicate pages to primary oncall
ops-bot: action: muted alert TenantHighErrorRate for tenant=acme-corp in prod for 2h (muted by marie). Ticketed as followup: PI-4321
ajay: creating dashboard: per-tenant 5xx rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, request_size_p50/p95. dashboard id: dash-Tenant-PI-4321
ajay: dashboard panels: tenant_5xx_rate, tenant_kv_cache_hit, tenant_avg_request_tokens
marie: runbook checklist for handoff -> siva: 1) verify mute is in place and expiration set 2) watch dashboard for next 3 hours 3) if error rate drops, plan threshold bump PR 4) if not, escalate to infra for host-level investigation
siva: taking handoff. I'll also kick off a canary run against acme-corp routing to reproduce locally: `/internal/canary?tenant=acme-corp&load=low`
siva: temp mitigation: lowering alert sensitivity for tenants <100rps to avoid future noisy pages; will add as filter in rule
product-ops: pinging CS: "We've placed monitoring and temporary mitigation; investigating root cause. No SLA breach declared yet, but we're watching closely."
marie: please create an SLA-impact assessment doc in PI-4321 with timeline and customer-facing notes. If we see sustained 5xx > 1% for 30m we escalate to SOC/Sales ops
ajay: pushed initial branch refs/changes/alert/PI-4321, PR pending: rfr/eng-sre/alert/PI-4321 (includes filter and min-rps guard)
ops-bot: ops note: applied prom rule patch to staging, running rule tests: PASS
marie: scheduling a post-incident tuning meeting tomorrow 10:00 PST to review dashboard + finalize permanent thresholds and exclusions
incbot: NOTE: paging suppressed (muted) — followups scheduled in PI-4321
siva: will post a short postmortem and the alert-rule PR once merged. I'll keep oncall watch for next 6 hours
marie: leaving oncall to siva. Summary: noisy tenant-specific page -> muted temporary -> propose threshold bump + min-rps guard + exclude internal tenants -> dashboard + ticket + handoff. Team react when you see this :thumbsup:
ajay: noted, will validate post-merge and monitor metrics for 24h
product-ops: adding a CS follow-up template to the ticket so support can send an update if customer asks
marie: thanks all. Good coordination.
